## Historical audit — S0331

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/test/bw_0039/1/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to its JSONL lines and supplied character ranges.

| Evidence | Observed operations and results |
|---|---|
| Goal and first build — H request line 1 [0,14340); H response line 3 [0,11977) | The requested goal was a separate-mesh reconstruction of a single indoor photograph. H interpreted it as a renovation room containing framing, masonry, a window, ladder, electrical box, lamp, and debris. Code emitted named assets and child parts, colored surfaces, camera and lights. These descriptions are H’s interpretation, not independent inspection of the reference. |
| Validation and revision — lines 9 [0,32615), 11 [0,60862), 13–14 [0,12530), [0,12283) | Step 1 built and rendered successfully. Its printed window upper-left projection was (0.509, 0.372), versus H’s estimated reference (0.63, 0.10). Given the reference and rendered image in the next request, H reported a small, low window, obstructing right wall, near-vertical ladder and pale lighting. It moved the rear wall, changed camera aim, altered ladder pose, and darkened surfaces and lighting. These visual diagnoses are H’s claims. |
| Exploration and second result — lines 19 [0,39248), 23–24 [0,13578), [0,13330) | Step 2 succeeded; baseline, trial and final projections showed the selected points moving right and upward with the aim change. H then reported remaining enclosure, window, ladder and lighting discrepancies. It preserved the camera, extended walls, enlarged the window and ladder, raised the lamp and changed debris to flat strips. This was iterative student exploration, not a demonstrated unique causal diagnosis. |
| Final result — lines 26, 28–30 [0,1548), [0,1538), [0,41306), [0,59) | Step 3 built and rendered successfully and was selected. Its window-corner projections were approximately (0.623, 0.133) and (0.899, 0.458), against estimated references (0.63, 0.10) and (0.92, 0.43). The foreground floor point remained (0.151, 0.886) versus (0.25, 0.98). These are point calculations, not visibility or silhouette checks. No subsequent student review or independent visual assessment is shown. |

**Scene checks and uncertainty.** Multiple distinct assets and colored material approximations are evident in code; masonry joints and lath are geometry rather than independently verified textures. Ladder rails, steps, hinges and spreaders are grouped and positioned as parts, but actual connections and pose fidelity are unverified. H’s reported camera, lighting, crop and occlusion problems motivated changes; the final render’s appearance and whether those changes fixed them remain unknown. The supplied observations contain image paths, not inspectable image pixels.

**Teacher input:** No separate teacher intervention, diagnosis, proposed update, or receipt is visible. The user/system instructions and subsequent runner feedback were received by H; revisions show use of the requested comparison and projection workflow, not adoption of unseen teacher advice. Session records show no autonomous external tool calls; Blender executions were runner events (lines 2, 12, 22; lines 4–9, 14–19, 24–29).

**Outcome and lessons.** Formal execution succeeded three times; reconstruction correctness is **unknown**, not established by successful rendering or selection. There is no empty patch, observed algorithm failure, or technical interruption. Transferably, separating projected landmarks from image appearance and testing camera direction makes discrepancies traceable. The particular room dimensions, ladder pose and lighting corrections are task-specific hypotheses, whose final visual and geometric validity remains unresolved.
